newsitem.title: USA: TRW says space, auto Q4 oper profit rose.
newsitem.headline: TRW says space, auto Q4 oper profit rose.

text.p: TRW Inc said on Tuesday fourth quarter operating profit in its space and defense segment rose five percent from a year ago, excluding special items.

Including special items, including a $19 million boost from recovery of certain tax costs and because 1995 included a reserve, space/defense operating profit rose to $81.1 million from $39.1 million, the maker of satellite systems and other high-tech products said.
Space/defense sales rose to $839.3 million from $724.8 million, mainly through recent contract awards, it said.
In its automotive business, excluding special items, operating profit rose to $154.5 million from $145.8 million.
That does not include a $41.5 million negative impact, mainly for warranty reserves, TRW said in a statement.
It said auto segment sales were $1.61 billion versus $1.59 billion. Air bag, steering and all product lines' volume rose, partly offset by lower pricing and foreign exchange rates.

For the year, Cleveland-based TRW said space/defense operating profit, excluding the special items, rose to $247.1 million from $222.2 million. Sales in the segment rose 8.5 percent to a record $3.36 billion from 1995's $3.10 billion.
It said 1996 automotive operating profits, excluding the special items, rose to $608.5 million from $607.2 million on record sales of $6.49 billion versus $6.47 billion.

As reported, TRW earned $0.97 a diluted share in the quarter versus $0.84 and, for the year, $3.60 versus $3.31. That reflects a $1.95 after-tax gain for the year from the sale of the information services business (including $0.13 fourth quarter) and a $1.89 charge (also $0.13 fourth quarter) for "actions to enhance the company's competitiveness."
A spokesman declined to elaborate on the actions.
"Supported by good economies, we expect to have another very good year in 1997," chairman and chief executive officer Joseph Gorman said in the statement.
